description: Reduce and interpret gravity survey data from raw readings through Bouguer anomaly computation, regional-residual separation, forward modeling, and inversion to produce a subsurface density interpretation.

steps.description: Apply instrument drift, tidal, latitude, and elevation corrections to raw gravity readings to produce reduced gravity values.

inputs.name: raw-gravity-readings
inputs.desc: Station-by-station gravity meter readings with timestamps and coordinates

inputs.name: base-station-ties
inputs.desc: Repeated base station readings for drift correction

inputs.name: station-elevations
inputs.desc: Surveyed elevations and coordinates for each station

outputs.name: reduced-gravity-values
outputs.desc: Gravity values corrected for drift, tides, latitude, and free-air effect

outputs.name: reduction-log
outputs.desc: Record of each correction applied and its magnitude

process: Compute instrument drift from base station repeats and apply a linear or polynomial correction
Remove tidal gravity variations using a tide prediction model for the survey dates and location
Apply latitude correction (normal gravity formula) and free-air correction using surveyed elevations
Tabulate the corrected values with station IDs and coordinates

steps.description: Compute Bouguer anomaly by applying the Bouguer slab and terrain corrections to the reduced gravity values.

inputs.name: reduced-gravity-values
inputs.desc: Gravity values after drift, tidal, latitude, and free-air corrections

inputs.name: terrain-model
inputs.desc: Digital elevation model surrounding the survey area

outputs.name: bouguer-anomaly-map
outputs.desc: Map of Bouguer anomaly values at each station

outputs.name: terrain-correction-values
outputs.desc: Terrain correction computed for each station

process: Apply the Bouguer slab correction using an assumed near-surface density (typically 2.67 g/cc)
Compute terrain corrections using the DEM for near-zone and far-zone topographic effects
Subtract the normal gravity field to obtain the Bouguer anomaly at each station
Grid the anomaly values and produce a contour map

steps.description: Separate the Bouguer anomaly into regional (deep) and residual (shallow) components using polynomial fitting or spectral filtering.

inputs.name: bouguer-anomaly-map
inputs.desc: Gridded Bouguer anomaly values

inputs.name: separation-parameters
inputs.desc: Method choice (polynomial order, filter cutoff wavelength)

outputs.name: regional-field
outputs.desc: Long-wavelength component representing deep structure

outputs.name: residual-anomaly
outputs.desc: Short-wavelength component representing shallow targets

process: Select the separation method (polynomial surface fitting, upward continuation, or bandpass filter)
Fit the regional field to the Bouguer anomaly grid
Subtract the regional from the Bouguer anomaly to obtain the residual
Validate that the residual highlights known shallow features and the regional is geologically reasonable

steps.description: Build a forward model of subsurface density structures and compute their predicted gravity response for comparison with the observed anomaly.

inputs.name: residual-anomaly
inputs.desc: Residual gravity anomaly highlighting shallow targets

inputs.name: geological-constraints
inputs.desc: Known geology, drill holes, seismic sections, or density measurements

outputs.name: forward-model-geometry
outputs.desc: 3D geometry of modeled density bodies

outputs.name: predicted-anomaly
outputs.desc: Gravity anomaly predicted by the forward model

process: Define initial body geometries using geological constraints (known contacts, faults, intrusions)
Assign density contrasts to each body based on rock property measurements or literature values
Compute the gravity response of each body and sum to produce the predicted anomaly
Compare predicted vs observed anomaly to identify where the model needs adjustment

steps.description: Invert the gravity anomaly to recover subsurface density distribution, refining the forward model geometry to match observations within data uncertainty.

inputs.name: residual-anomaly
inputs.desc: Observed residual gravity anomaly

inputs.name: forward-model-geometry
inputs.desc: Initial model geometry from forward modeling

outputs.name: inverted-density-model
outputs.desc: Subsurface density distribution that fits the observed anomaly

outputs.name: misfit-report
outputs.desc: RMS misfit between observed and modeled anomaly, with residual map

process: Set up the inversion mesh and assign initial density values from the forward model
Select the inversion algorithm (smooth, compact, or constrained by geological boundaries)
Run the inversion, iterating until the data misfit reaches the target threshold
Evaluate the result for geological plausibility and quantify non-uniqueness

steps.description: Synthesize all gravity analysis products into an interpretation report with figures, depth estimates, and geological conclusions.

inputs.name: inverted-density-model
inputs.desc: Final subsurface density model from inversion

inputs.name: misfit-report
inputs.desc: Data misfit and residual analysis

inputs.name: bouguer-anomaly-map
inputs.desc: Original Bouguer anomaly map for reference

outputs.name: gravity-report
outputs.desc: Interpretation report with figures, cross-sections, depth estimates, and conclusions

outputs.name: data-archive
outputs.desc: Packaged data, models, and processing logs for reproducibility

process: Compile cross-sections through the density model at key profiles
Annotate with depth estimates and geological unit assignments
Write the interpretation narrative linking the gravity results to the geological question
Package all data, scripts, and intermediate products for archival

description: Process and interpret magnetic survey data from raw readings through diurnal correction, reduction to pole, source identification, depth estimation, and subsurface modeling.

steps.description: Apply diurnal correction and remove the International Geomagnetic Reference Field (IGRF) from raw total-field magnetic readings.

inputs.name: raw-magnetic-readings
inputs.desc: Total-field magnetometer readings with timestamps and coordinates

inputs.name: base-station-magnetogram
inputs.desc: Continuous base station magnetic record for diurnal correction

outputs.name: corrected-magnetic-anomaly
outputs.desc: Magnetic anomaly after diurnal and IGRF removal

outputs.name: processing-log
outputs.desc: Record of corrections applied

process: Subtract diurnal variations using the base station magnetogram aligned to survey timestamps
Remove the IGRF reference field for the survey date and location
Flag and handle any despiking needed for cultural noise or instrument glitches
Grid the anomaly values for mapping

steps.description: Transform the magnetic anomaly to what it would look like at the magnetic north pole, centering anomalies over their sources.

inputs.name: corrected-magnetic-anomaly
inputs.desc: Gridded magnetic anomaly after diurnal and IGRF removal

inputs.name: field-parameters
inputs.desc: Magnetic inclination and declination at the survey location

outputs.name: rtp-anomaly
outputs.desc: Reduced-to-pole magnetic anomaly grid

outputs.name: rtp-quality-check
outputs.desc: Comparison of original and RTP anomaly shapes to verify the transformation

process: Compute the reduction-to-pole operator in the frequency domain using the local field direction
Apply the operator to the gridded anomaly, handling low-latitude instability if needed
Compare anomaly shapes before and after RTP to confirm sources are now centered under their anomalies
Document the field parameters and any stabilization applied

steps.description: Identify individual magnetic sources from the RTP anomaly using derivative analysis, analytic signal, and tilt angle methods.

inputs.name: rtp-anomaly
inputs.desc: Reduced-to-pole magnetic anomaly grid

inputs.name: geological-context
inputs.desc: Known geology and expected magnetic rock types

outputs.name: source-catalog
outputs.desc: List of identified magnetic sources with locations and anomaly characteristics

outputs.name: derivative-maps
outputs.desc: First vertical derivative, analytic signal, and tilt angle maps

process: Compute the first vertical derivative to sharpen source edges
Compute the analytic signal amplitude to locate source centers regardless of magnetization direction
Apply the tilt angle method to delineate source boundaries
Catalog each distinct source with its location, amplitude, wavelength, and geological interpretation

steps.description: Estimate depth to magnetic sources using Euler deconvolution, Werner deconvolution, or spectral depth analysis.

inputs.name: rtp-anomaly
inputs.desc: Reduced-to-pole magnetic anomaly grid

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: Identified magnetic sources with locations

outputs.name: depth-estimates
outputs.desc: Depth to each source with uncertainty ranges

outputs.name: depth-method-comparison
outputs.desc: Cross-comparison of depths from multiple methods

process: Run Euler deconvolution with structural indices for contacts, dikes, and spheres
Apply Werner deconvolution along selected profiles crossing key anomalies
Use radially averaged power spectrum for average depth to magnetic basement
Compare depth estimates from each method and assign confidence based on agreement

steps.description: Build forward and inverse models of subsurface magnetic bodies that fit the observed anomaly within data uncertainty.

inputs.name: rtp-anomaly
inputs.desc: Observed RTP anomaly for model comparison

inputs.name: depth-estimates
inputs.desc: Depth constraints from Euler and Werner methods

inputs.name: geological-context
inputs.desc: Known geology and rock property data

outputs.name: magnetic-model
outputs.desc: Geometry and susceptibility of modeled magnetic bodies

outputs.name: model-fit-report
outputs.desc: Observed vs modeled anomaly profiles with misfit statistics

process: Define initial body geometries using depth estimates and geological constraints
Assign susceptibility values from rock property measurements or literature
Forward-model and adjust geometry to minimize misfit along key profiles
Run a 3D inversion if profile modeling is insufficient

steps.description: Compile magnetic survey results into an interpretation report with maps, depth sections, source models, and geological conclusions.

inputs.name: magnetic-model
inputs.desc: Final subsurface magnetic model

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: Catalog of identified magnetic sources

inputs.name: model-fit-report
inputs.desc: Misfit analysis and model quality assessment

outputs.name: magnetics-report
outputs.desc: Interpretation report with maps, sections, and conclusions

outputs.name: magnetics-data-archive
outputs.desc: All data, models, and processing files packaged for reproducibility

process: Compile anomaly maps, derivative products, and depth estimates into coherent figure panels
Draw cross-sections through the magnetic model at key profiles
Write the geological interpretation linking magnetic results to the survey objectives
Package all data and processing workflows for archival

description: Analyze tree-ring data from ring-width measurement through crossdating, standardization, chronology building, climate correlation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.

steps.description: Measure ring widths from prepared core or cross-section samples under a stereomicroscope with a measuring stage.

inputs.name: prepared-samples
inputs.desc: Sanded tree cores or cross-sections mounted for measurement

inputs.name: measurement-setup
inputs.desc: Stage calibration, software, and measurement protocol

outputs.name: raw-ring-widths
outputs.desc: Annual ring-width measurements for each sample in standard format (Tucson decadal)

outputs.name: sample-metadata
outputs.desc: Species, site, core ID, and measurement notes for each sample

process: Verify sample surface preparation is adequate for ring boundary visibility
Calibrate the measuring stage and set the resolution
Measure each ring from pith to bark, recording widths in the standard Tucson decadal format
Flag any problematic rings (false rings, missing rings, compression wood) for crossdating attention

steps.description: Crossdate each sample series against the master chronology to verify that every ring is assigned to the correct calendar year.

inputs.name: raw-ring-widths
inputs.desc: Measured ring-width series for all samples

inputs.name: master-chronology
inputs.desc: Existing site or regional master chronology for the species

outputs.name: crossdated-series
outputs.desc: Ring-width series with verified calendar year assignments

outputs.name: crossdating-statistics
outputs.desc: Correlation statistics, t-values, and flagged segments for each sample

process: Run COFECHA or equivalent to compute segment correlations against the master chronology
Identify segments with low correlation and check visually for missing or false rings
Insert or remove rings as needed and re-verify until all segments pass quality thresholds
Document all dating corrections with justification

steps.description: Remove the biological age trend from ring-width series to isolate the climate signal, producing dimensionless index values.

inputs.name: crossdated-series
inputs.desc: Verified annual ring-width series

inputs.name: detrending-method
inputs.desc: Choice of detrending curve (negative exponential, spline, regional curve standardization)

outputs.name: standardized-indices
outputs.desc: Dimensionless ring-width index series for each sample

outputs.name: detrending-parameters
outputs.desc: Fitted curve type and parameters for each series

process: Fit the chosen detrending function to each raw ring-width series
Divide the measured width by the fitted value to produce a dimensionless index
Inspect each standardized series for residual non-climatic trends
Document the detrending method and any manual adjustments

steps.description: Combine standardized individual series into a site chronology using a biweight robust mean, and assess signal strength.

inputs.name: standardized-indices
inputs.desc: Standardized ring-width indices for all samples at the site

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Sample counts and date ranges

outputs.name: site-chronology
outputs.desc: Mean site chronology with sample depth and confidence intervals

outputs.name: signal-strength-statistics
outputs.desc: Expressed population signal (EPS), running Rbar, and sample depth over time

process: Compute the biweight robust mean of all standardized series for each year
Calculate the running EPS and Rbar to assess where the chronology has adequate signal strength
Truncate the chronology where EPS falls below the 0.85 threshold
Plot the final chronology with sample depth and EPS over time

steps.description: Correlate the site chronology with instrumental climate records to identify which climate variables the tree rings respond to.

inputs.name: site-chronology
inputs.desc: Final site chronology

inputs.name: climate-records
inputs.desc: Monthly or seasonal temperature, precipitation, and drought index records for the region

outputs.name: correlation-results
outputs.desc: Monthly and seasonal correlation coefficients with significance tests

outputs.name: response-function
outputs.desc: Bootstrap response function showing the climate window the trees respond to

process: Compute Pearson correlations between the chronology and each monthly climate variable over the calibration period
Run a bootstrap response function analysis to assess stability of the correlations
Identify the seasonal window with the strongest and most stable correlation
Test for temporal instability in the growth-climate relationship

steps.description: Use the calibrated growth-climate relationship to reconstruct the climate variable back through the full length of the tree-ring chronology.

inputs.name: site-chronology
inputs.desc: Full tree-ring chronology

inputs.name: correlation-results
inputs.desc: Calibrated growth-climate relationship and optimal season

outputs.name: climate-reconstruction
outputs.desc: Reconstructed climate variable with uncertainty envelope for the full chronology period

outputs.name: verification-statistics
outputs.desc: Split-period calibration-verification results (RE, CE, r-squared)

process: Build the transfer function using linear regression or scaling over the calibration period
Validate using a split-period or leave-one-out cross-validation
Compute reduction of error (RE) and coefficient of efficiency (CE) statistics
Apply the transfer function to the full chronology and attach the reconstruction uncertainty envelope

steps.description: Compile the dendrochronology analysis into a report with chronology plots, climate correlations, and the paleoclimate reconstruction.

inputs.name: climate-reconstruction
inputs.desc: Final paleoclimate reconstruction with uncertainty

inputs.name: verification-statistics
inputs.desc: Calibration and verification results

inputs.name: signal-strength-statistics
inputs.desc: EPS and Rbar over time

outputs.name: dendro-report
outputs.desc: Full analysis report with figures, statistics, and interpretation

outputs.name: dendro-data-archive
outputs.desc: Ring-width data, chronology, and reconstruction in standard formats

process: Assemble figures showing the chronology, climate correlations, and reconstruction
Write the methods section detailing each processing step and parameter choice
Interpret the reconstruction in the context of regional climate history
Format the data files in standard formats (ITRDB) for archival

description: Characterize a semiconductor device or material through I-V measurement, C-V analysis, Hall effect measurement, defect assessment, and a compiled device report.

steps.description: Measure current-voltage characteristics of the semiconductor device to extract threshold voltage, transconductance, and on-off ratio.

inputs.name: device-under-test
inputs.desc: Semiconductor device or test structure with probe contacts

inputs.name: measurement-conditions
inputs.desc: Temperature, sweep range, compliance, and step size

outputs.name: iv-data
outputs.desc: Current-voltage curves (transfer and output characteristics)

outputs.name: extracted-parameters
outputs.desc: Threshold voltage, transconductance, on-off ratio, subthreshold swing

process: Set up the probe station and source-measure unit with the specified sweep parameters
Measure the transfer characteristic (Id vs Vg at fixed Vd) for threshold and transconductance extraction
Measure the output characteristic (Id vs Vd at multiple Vg) for saturation and linearity assessment
Extract the key device parameters using standard methods (linear extrapolation, max-gm)

steps.description: Perform capacitance-voltage analysis to extract the doping profile, oxide thickness, and flatband voltage of the semiconductor structure.

inputs.name: device-under-test
inputs.desc: MOS capacitor or gated device for C-V measurement

inputs.name: cv-measurement-conditions
inputs.desc: Frequency, AC signal amplitude, DC sweep range, temperature

outputs.name: cv-data
outputs.desc: Capacitance vs voltage curves at one or more frequencies

outputs.name: doping-profile
outputs.desc: Extracted doping concentration vs depth profile

process: Measure C-V curve from accumulation through inversion at the specified frequency
Extract oxide capacitance from the accumulation region
Compute the doping profile from the slope of the 1/C-squared vs V plot
Check for frequency dispersion (compare curves at multiple frequencies) as a quality indicator

steps.description: Measure the Hall effect to determine carrier concentration, carrier type (n or p), and Hall mobility of the semiconductor material.

inputs.name: hall-sample
inputs.desc: Semiconductor sample in van der Pauw or Hall bar geometry

inputs.name: hall-conditions
inputs.desc: Magnetic field strength, current level, temperature

outputs.name: hall-data
outputs.desc: Hall voltage measurements and sheet resistance values

outputs.name: carrier-properties
outputs.desc: Carrier type, carrier concentration, and Hall mobility

process: Measure the sheet resistance using the van der Pauw method with current reversal and contact averaging
Apply the magnetic field and measure the Hall voltage with current and field reversals to eliminate offsets
Compute the Hall coefficient, carrier concentration, and carrier type from the sign of the Hall voltage
Calculate the Hall mobility from the ratio of Hall coefficient to resistivity

steps.description: Assess defect density in the semiconductor using deep-level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) or photoluminescence (PL) to identify trap levels.

inputs.name: device-under-test
inputs.desc: Semiconductor device or sample prepared for DLTS or PL

inputs.name: defect-measurement-conditions
inputs.desc: Temperature range, rate windows (DLTS) or excitation wavelength (PL)

outputs.name: defect-spectrum
outputs.desc: DLTS peaks or PL spectrum identifying defect energy levels

outputs.name: trap-parameters
outputs.desc: Activation energy, capture cross-section, and trap density for each identified level

process: For DLTS: sweep temperature while recording capacitance transients at selected rate windows
Construct the DLTS spectrum (peak height vs temperature) and identify distinct trap levels
Extract activation energy and capture cross-section from an Arrhenius plot of the emission rate
For PL: measure emission spectrum at cryogenic temperature and assign peaks to known defect transitions

steps.description: Compile all characterization results into a device report with parameter tables, comparison to specifications, and a quality assessment.

inputs.name: extracted-parameters
inputs.desc: I-V parameters (threshold, gm, on-off)

inputs.name: doping-profile
inputs.desc: Doping concentration vs depth from C-V

inputs.name: carrier-properties
inputs.desc: Carrier type, concentration, and mobility from Hall

inputs.name: trap-parameters
inputs.desc: Identified defect levels and densities

outputs.name: semiconductor-report
outputs.desc: Full characterization report with parameter tables, figures, and conclusions

outputs.name: characterization-data-package
outputs.desc: All raw data and extracted parameters for archival

process: Tabulate all extracted parameters alongside target specifications
Generate standard figures (I-V curves, C-V curves, doping profile, DLTS spectrum)
Compare results to the design target or published literature values
Write the conclusions and identify any performance or defect concerns

description: Analyze ocean current data from ADCP or drifter measurements through quality control, tidal decomposition, circulation pattern identification, validation, and reporting.

steps.description: Quality-control raw ADCP or drifter current measurements by removing outliers, correcting for magnetic deviation, and flagging suspect data.

inputs.name: raw-current-data
inputs.desc: ADCP profiles or drifter positions and velocities with timestamps

inputs.name: magnetic-declination
inputs.desc: Local magnetic declination for compass correction

outputs.name: qc-current-data
outputs.desc: Quality-controlled current velocities with flags

outputs.name: qc-report
outputs.desc: Summary of data removed, flagged, and corrected

process: Apply magnetic declination correction to convert magnetic to true north
Remove data below the echo amplitude or correlation thresholds (ADCP) or fix obvious position jumps (drifters)
Flag outliers using speed thresholds and temporal consistency checks
Compute basic statistics (mean speed, direction, data return) for the quality-controlled dataset

steps.description: Separate the current time series into tidal and residual (non-tidal) components using harmonic analysis.

inputs.name: qc-current-data
inputs.desc: Quality-controlled current velocities

inputs.name: tidal-constituents
inputs.desc: List of tidal constituents to fit (M2, S2, K1, O1, etc.)

outputs.name: tidal-current
outputs.desc: Predicted tidal current from the fitted harmonics

outputs.name: residual-current
outputs.desc: Non-tidal residual current after removing the tidal prediction

outputs.name: tidal-ellipse-parameters
outputs.desc: Semi-major axis, eccentricity, inclination, and phase for each constituent

process: Perform harmonic analysis on the east and north velocity components using t_tide or UTide
Extract tidal ellipse parameters for each resolved constituent
Subtract the tidal prediction from the observed current to produce the residual
Validate the decomposition by checking explained variance and residual spectrum

steps.description: Identify dominant circulation patterns in the residual current using EOF analysis, progressive vector diagrams, and seasonal statistics.

inputs.name: residual-current
inputs.desc: Non-tidal residual current velocities

inputs.name: wind-and-pressure-data
inputs.desc: Concurrent wind and atmospheric pressure records for forcing analysis

outputs.name: circulation-patterns
outputs.desc: Dominant modes of variability, progressive vector diagrams, and seasonal statistics

outputs.name: forcing-correlations
outputs.desc: Correlations between residual current and wind/pressure forcing

process: Compute progressive vector diagrams to visualize net transport direction and magnitude
Run EOF analysis on multi-depth current profiles to identify dominant vertical modes
Compute seasonal mean current roses and statistics
Correlate residual current with wind speed, direction, and atmospheric pressure to identify forcing mechanisms

steps.description: Validate in-situ current measurements against satellite-derived surface currents from altimetry.

inputs.name: qc-current-data
inputs.desc: In-situ surface current measurements

inputs.name: altimetry-data
inputs.desc: Satellite-derived geostrophic surface current for the measurement area

outputs.name: validation-statistics
outputs.desc: Bias, RMSE, and correlation between in-situ and satellite currents

outputs.name: validation-figures
outputs.desc: Time series comparison and scatter plots

process: Extract the satellite geostrophic current at the in-situ measurement location
Compare surface layer in-situ current with satellite current using concurrent time windows
Compute bias, RMSE, and correlation coefficient for each velocity component
Identify systematic differences and their likely causes (ageostrophic flow, spatial resolution)

steps.description: Compile the ocean current analysis into a report with current maps, tidal ellipses, circulation patterns, and conclusions.

inputs.name: tidal-ellipse-parameters
inputs.desc: Tidal constituent results

inputs.name: circulation-patterns
inputs.desc: Residual current analysis results

inputs.name: validation-statistics
inputs.desc: Satellite validation results

outputs.name: current-report
outputs.desc: Current analysis report with figures, statistics, and conclusions

outputs.name: current-data-archive
outputs.desc: All data and processing files packaged for reproducibility

process: Compile tidal ellipse maps, current roses, and progressive vector diagrams into figure panels
Summarize the dominant circulation patterns and their forcing mechanisms
Discuss the validation results and data quality assessment
Package all data and processing scripts for archival

description: Characterize material rheology through geometry selection, steady-shear and oscillatory measurements, linear viscoelastic region determination, constitutive model fitting, and reporting.

steps.description: Select the appropriate measurement geometry (cone-plate, parallel plate, Couette) based on the material's viscosity range and sample constraints.

inputs.name: sample-description
inputs.desc: Material type, expected viscosity range, and available sample volume

inputs.name: instrument-capabilities
inputs.desc: Available geometries, torque range, and gap control

outputs.name: selected-geometry
outputs.desc: Chosen geometry with dimensions and gap setting

outputs.name: loading-protocol
outputs.desc: Sample loading and conditioning procedure

process: Assess the viscosity range to choose between cone-plate (low-medium), parallel plate (soft solids, gels), or Couette (low viscosity liquids)
Select the geometry dimensions based on sample volume and torque sensitivity requirements
Define the sample loading procedure including any pre-shear or rest time
Document the temperature control method and any solvent trap needed

steps.description: Measure the steady-state shear viscosity as a function of shear rate to characterize shear-thinning, shear-thickening, or Newtonian behavior.

inputs.name: loaded-sample
inputs.desc: Material loaded in the selected geometry, conditioned and at temperature

inputs.name: shear-rate-range
inputs.desc: Shear rate sweep range and number of points

outputs.name: flow-curve-data
outputs.desc: Viscosity and shear stress vs shear rate

outputs.name: flow-behavior-classification
outputs.desc: Newtonian, shear-thinning, shear-thickening, or yield stress behavior

process: Run a logarithmic shear rate sweep from low to high rates with steady-state detection at each point
Verify time independence by running a reverse sweep (high to low) and checking for hysteresis
Plot viscosity vs shear rate on log-log axes and shear stress vs shear rate
Classify the flow behavior and identify the zero-shear viscosity and power-law region if applicable

steps.description: Perform an oscillatory amplitude sweep to determine the linear viscoelastic region (LVER) of the material.

inputs.name: loaded-sample
inputs.desc: Material loaded and conditioned in the geometry

inputs.name: amplitude-sweep-parameters
inputs.desc: Frequency to hold constant, strain or stress amplitude range

outputs.name: amplitude-sweep-data
outputs.desc: Storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G'') vs strain amplitude

outputs.name: lver-limit
outputs.desc: Critical strain marking the end of the linear viscoelastic region

process: Run a logarithmic strain amplitude sweep at a fixed frequency (typically 1 Hz)
Plot G' and G'' vs strain amplitude and identify the plateau region
Determine the critical strain where G' drops by 5% from the plateau value
Record the LVER limit for use in frequency sweep measurements

steps.description: Measure storage and loss moduli as a function of frequency within the LVER to characterize the viscoelastic spectrum.

inputs.name: loaded-sample
inputs.desc: Material loaded and conditioned

inputs.name: frequency-sweep-parameters
inputs.desc: Strain amplitude (within LVER), frequency range

inputs.name: lver-limit
inputs.desc: Critical strain from the amplitude sweep to set the measurement strain below

outputs.name: frequency-sweep-data
outputs.desc: G', G'', complex viscosity, and tan(delta) vs frequency

outputs.name: viscoelastic-classification
outputs.desc: Material behavior type: liquid-like, gel-like, or solid-like with crossover frequency if present

process: Set the strain amplitude below the LVER limit
Run a logarithmic frequency sweep from high to low frequency
Plot G' and G'' vs frequency and identify crossover points, plateaus, and terminal zone behavior
Classify the material and check Cox-Merz rule agreement with steady-shear data

steps.description: Fit the rheological data to a constitutive model (Cross, Carreau, Herschel-Bulkley, Maxwell) to extract material parameters.

inputs.name: flow-curve-data
inputs.desc: Steady-shear viscosity vs shear rate

inputs.name: frequency-sweep-data
inputs.desc: G' and G'' vs frequency

outputs.name: fitted-model-parameters
outputs.desc: Best-fit model parameters with confidence intervals

outputs.name: model-fit-quality
outputs.desc: Residual plots and goodness-of-fit statistics

process: Select candidate constitutive models based on the observed flow behavior
Fit each candidate to the steady-shear and/or oscillatory data using nonlinear regression
Compare models by residual analysis and information criteria (AIC or BIC)
Report the best-fit parameters with 95% confidence intervals

steps.description: Compile the rheological characterization into a report with flow curves, viscoelastic spectra, model fits, and material classification.

inputs.name: flow-curve-data
inputs.desc: Steady-shear flow curve

inputs.name: frequency-sweep-data
inputs.desc: Oscillatory frequency sweep data

inputs.name: fitted-model-parameters
inputs.desc: Constitutive model fit results

outputs.name: rheology-characterization-report
outputs.desc: Full rheology report with figures, tables, and material classification

outputs.name: rheology-data-package
outputs.desc: All raw data, processed curves, and model fits for archival

process: Generate publication-quality figures for flow curve, amplitude sweep, and frequency sweep
Tabulate the material parameters and model fit results
Compare to published data for similar materials if available
Write conclusions about material behavior relevant to the application

description: Analyze ancient DNA from specimen extraction through library preparation, sequencing, endogenous content filtering, reference mapping, authentication, and reporting.

steps.description: Extract DNA from ancient specimens (bone, tooth, sediment) using protocols optimized for short, damaged fragments.

inputs.name: ancient-specimen
inputs.desc: Bone powder, tooth root, or sediment sample prepared under clean-room conditions

inputs.name: extraction-protocol
inputs.desc: Selected protocol (silica column, magnetic bead) with blank controls

outputs.name: dna-extract
outputs.desc: Purified DNA extract ready for library preparation

outputs.name: extraction-log
outputs.desc: Weights, volumes, incubation times, and blank control results

process: Process the specimen in a dedicated ancient DNA clean room with UV-sterilized equipment
Run the lysis, binding, and elution steps per the selected protocol
Process extraction blanks alongside every batch to monitor contamination
Quantify the extract with a fluorometric assay (Qubit or equivalent)

steps.description: Prepare sequencing libraries from the aDNA extract using damage-aware protocols that preserve the short, degraded fragments.

inputs.name: dna-extract
inputs.desc: Purified ancient DNA extract

inputs.name: library-protocol
inputs.desc: Single-stranded or double-stranded library protocol with UDG treatment option

outputs.name: sequencing-library
outputs.desc: Indexed sequencing library ready for capture or shotgun sequencing

outputs.name: library-metrics
outputs.desc: Molecule count, complexity estimate, and fragment length distribution

process: Perform end repair and adapter ligation using a protocol suited to short fragments
Add unique dual indexes for downstream demultiplexing and contamination tracking
Amplify with minimal PCR cycles to preserve library complexity
QC the library on a fragment analyzer to verify the size distribution

steps.description: Sequence the library and filter reads for endogenous content, removing modern contamination and low-quality sequences.

inputs.name: sequencing-library
inputs.desc: Indexed aDNA library on the sequencer

inputs.name: reference-genome
inputs.desc: Target reference genome for alignment

outputs.name: filtered-alignments
outputs.desc: BAM file of quality-filtered, deduplicated alignments to the reference

outputs.name: endogenous-content-report
outputs.desc: Percent endogenous, duplication rate, and coverage statistics

process: Demultiplex and trim adapters from the raw sequencing reads
Align to the reference genome with a mapper that handles short reads (BWA aln or equivalent)
Remove PCR duplicates and filter for mapping quality and minimum length
Compute endogenous content, coverage, and duplication rate

steps.description: Authenticate the ancient DNA by verifying characteristic damage patterns (C-to-T deamination at fragment ends) and fragment length distribution.

inputs.name: filtered-alignments
inputs.desc: Quality-filtered alignments to the reference genome

inputs.name: library-metrics
inputs.desc: Library preparation details (UDG treatment status)

outputs.name: damage-profile
outputs.desc: Misincorporation patterns at read ends showing the expected C-to-T enrichment

outputs.name: authentication-verdict
outputs.desc: Assessment of whether the DNA is authentically ancient based on damage and fragment patterns

process: Run mapDamage or DamageProfiler to compute misincorporation rates at each position from the read ends
Verify the expected C-to-T elevation at the 5-prime end (and G-to-A at 3-prime for non-UDG libraries)
Check that the fragment length distribution peaks in the 30-80 bp range typical of ancient DNA
Assess contamination estimates from the mitochondrial reads if sufficient coverage exists

steps.description: Analyze the authenticated aDNA data for population genetics, phylogenetic placement, or phenotype prediction, and compile the final report.

inputs.name: filtered-alignments
inputs.desc: Authenticated, quality-filtered alignments

inputs.name: authentication-verdict
inputs.desc: Confirmed ancient DNA authentication

inputs.name: endogenous-content-report
inputs.desc: Coverage and endogenous content statistics

outputs.name: adna-report
outputs.desc: Full ancient DNA analysis report with authentication evidence, population results, and interpretation

outputs.name: adna-data-archive
outputs.desc: Raw data, alignments, and analysis scripts packaged for repository submission

process: Call variants or genotype at diagnostic SNPs depending on coverage
Place the individual in a population genetic context (PCA, ADMIXTURE, f-statistics)
Interpret the results in the archaeological and historical context of the specimen
Package all data and scripts for submission to a public repository (ENA or SRA)

description: Process and interpret ground-penetrating radar data from raw radargrams through signal processing, velocity analysis, feature interpretation, validation, and reporting.

steps.description: Apply time-zero correction, gain functions, and frequency filtering to raw GPR radargrams.

inputs.name: raw-radargrams
inputs.desc: GPR profiles as time-domain traces with position markers

inputs.name: acquisition-parameters
inputs.desc: Antenna frequency, time window, sampling rate, and survey geometry

outputs.name: processed-radargrams
outputs.desc: Gain-corrected, filtered radargrams ready for interpretation

outputs.name: processing-log
outputs.desc: Record of all processing steps and parameters applied

process: Apply time-zero correction to align all traces to the ground surface
Apply a gain function (SEC or AGC) to compensate for geometric spreading and attenuation
Bandpass filter to remove low-frequency noise (wow) and high-frequency noise
Apply background removal to suppress horizontal banding from system ringing

steps.description: Estimate the subsurface radar wave velocity to convert two-way travel time to depth.

inputs.name: processed-radargrams
inputs.desc: Processed GPR profiles

inputs.name: calibration-targets
inputs.desc: Known buried objects or layer depths for velocity calibration

outputs.name: velocity-model
outputs.desc: Estimated velocity for each material layer or spatially variable velocity field

outputs.name: depth-converted-profiles
outputs.desc: GPR profiles converted from time to depth using the velocity model

process: Analyze hyperbola apexes from point targets to fit velocity using curve matching
Cross-reference with known target depths if calibration objects are available
Build a layered or spatially variable velocity model
Convert all profiles from two-way travel time to depth

steps.description: Migrate the GPR profiles to collapse diffraction hyperbolas and position reflectors at their true subsurface locations.

inputs.name: processed-radargrams
inputs.desc: Gain-corrected and filtered radargrams

inputs.name: velocity-model
inputs.desc: Subsurface velocity estimates for migration

outputs.name: migrated-profiles
outputs.desc: Migrated GPR profiles with diffractions collapsed and dipping reflectors repositioned

outputs.name: migration-quality-check
outputs.desc: Comparison of pre- and post-migration images at key features

process: Select the migration algorithm (Kirchhoff, Stolt, or finite-difference) based on data quality and velocity complexity
Apply migration using the estimated velocity model
Compare pre- and post-migration images to verify diffraction collapse
Adjust the velocity model and re-migrate if diffractions are under- or over-collapsed

steps.description: Interpret subsurface features from the processed GPR profiles, classifying reflectors as geological layers, buried structures, utilities, or voids.

inputs.name: depth-converted-profiles
inputs.desc: Depth-converted and migrated GPR profiles

inputs.name: site-context
inputs.desc: Known site history, expected targets, and surface conditions

outputs.name: feature-catalog
outputs.desc: Interpreted features with locations, depths, and classifications

outputs.name: interpretation-maps
outputs.desc: Plan-view maps of interpreted features across the survey area

process: Trace continuous reflectors across multiple profiles to identify layer boundaries
Classify point reflectors and hyperbolic patterns as utilities, boulders, or voids based on signature
Map feature locations and depths in plan view by connecting picks across parallel profiles
Assign confidence levels based on signal quality and consistency across profiles

steps.description: Validate GPR interpretations against ground truth from excavation, boring logs, or known reference targets.

inputs.name: feature-catalog
inputs.desc: Interpreted GPR features with predicted locations and depths

inputs.name: ground-truth-data
inputs.desc: Boring logs, excavation records, or known target locations

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Comparison of predicted vs actual feature locations with accuracy statistics

outputs.name: depth-accuracy-assessment
outputs.desc: Depth error statistics and velocity model accuracy evaluation

process: Match each ground-truth feature to the nearest GPR interpretation
Compute horizontal and vertical position errors
Assess whether the velocity model produced accurate depths or needs refinement
Document any features detected by GPR but not confirmed, and vice versa

steps.description: Compile the GPR survey results into an interpretation report with annotated profiles, plan-view maps, and conclusions.

inputs.name: interpretation-maps
inputs.desc: Plan-view feature maps

inputs.name: feature-catalog
inputs.desc: Interpreted features with depths and classifications

inputs.name: validation-results
inputs.desc: Ground truth comparison results

outputs.name: gpr-report
outputs.desc: Full GPR survey report with annotated profiles, maps, and recommendations

outputs.name: gpr-data-archive
outputs.desc: All raw and processed data packaged for reproducibility

process: Annotate representative profile sections with feature picks and depth labels
Compile plan-view maps showing all interpreted features
Write the interpretation narrative addressing the survey objectives
Package all data files and processing parameters for archival

description: Date sediments by optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) or thermoluminescence (TL) from sample collection through mineral preparation, equivalent dose measurement, dose rate determination, age computation, and reporting.

steps.description: Collect sediment samples for luminescence dating under light-safe conditions and record the stratigraphic context.

inputs.name: sampling-site
inputs.desc: Exposed section or core with target dating horizons identified

inputs.name: sampling-protocol
inputs.desc: Opaque tube insertion method and field documentation requirements

outputs.name: collected-samples
outputs.desc: Sediment samples in opaque tubes with stratigraphic positions recorded

outputs.name: field-dosimetry-data
outputs.desc: In-situ gamma spectrometry or dosimeter placement records

process: Drive opaque metal or PVC tubes horizontally into the cleaned section face
Seal both ends immediately to prevent light exposure
Record the stratigraphic position, depth below surface, and water table level
Measure the field gamma dose rate with a portable spectrometer or install dosimeters

steps.description: Extract and prepare quartz or feldspar mineral grains from the sediment under safe-light conditions.

inputs.name: collected-samples
inputs.desc: Sediment samples in opaque tubes

inputs.name: target-mineral
inputs.desc: Quartz or feldspar, and target grain-size fraction

outputs.name: prepared-aliquots
outputs.desc: Mineral grains mounted on discs ready for measurement

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Grain size, etching time, density separation parameters, and yield

process: Open tubes under dim red or orange safe-light and discard the light-exposed ends
Wet sieve to isolate the target grain-size fraction (typically 90-250 microns)
Treat with HCl and H2O2 to remove carbonates and organics
Separate quartz from feldspar using heavy liquid density separation and etch quartz with HF

steps.description: Measure the equivalent dose (De) using the single-aliquot regenerative-dose (SAR) protocol on a luminescence reader.

inputs.name: prepared-aliquots
inputs.desc: Quartz or feldspar grains mounted on measurement discs

inputs.name: sar-protocol
inputs.desc: Preheat temperatures, regenerative dose steps, and test dose value

outputs.name: de-distribution
outputs.desc: Equivalent dose values for each aliquot with uncertainties

outputs.name: sar-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Recycling ratios, recuperation, and dose recovery test results

process: Run the SAR protocol: natural measurement, then a sequence of regenerative doses bracketing the expected De
Include a zero-dose and repeated-dose step to check recuperation and recycling ratio
Construct the dose-response curve for each aliquot and interpolate the natural signal to obtain De
Run dose recovery tests on a subset to verify the protocol accurately recovers a known dose

steps.description: Determine the environmental dose rate from radioelement concentrations, cosmic ray contribution, and water content.

inputs.name: field-dosimetry-data
inputs.desc: In-situ gamma spectrometry or dosimeter readings

inputs.name: sediment-chemistry
inputs.desc: Uranium, thorium, and potassium concentrations from lab analysis (ICP-MS or NAA)

outputs.name: total-dose-rate
outputs.desc: Total environmental dose rate in Gy/ka with uncertainty

outputs.name: dose-rate-components
outputs.desc: Alpha, beta, gamma, and cosmic dose rate contributions

process: Convert U, Th, and K concentrations to alpha, beta, and gamma dose rates using published conversion factors
Correct the beta dose rate for grain-size attenuation and the alpha dose rate for efficiency
Estimate the cosmic dose rate from burial depth and site latitude/altitude
Apply the water content correction and sum all components

steps.description: Compute the luminescence age from the equivalent dose and dose rate, assessing for complications like incomplete bleaching or dose rate changes.

inputs.name: de-distribution
inputs.desc: Equivalent dose values with uncertainties

inputs.name: total-dose-rate
inputs.desc: Environmental dose rate in Gy/ka

outputs.name: luminescence-age
outputs.desc: Calculated age in ka with total uncertainty

outputs.name: age-model-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of De distribution shape, overdispersion, and chosen age model (CAM, MAM, FMM)

process: Plot the De distribution and assess overdispersion relative to measurement uncertainty
Select the appropriate age model: central age model for well-bleached, minimum age model for partially bleached
Compute the age as De / dose rate and propagate all uncertainties
Compare the result with independent age control if available

steps.description: Compile the luminescence dating results into a report with stratigraphic context, measurement data, and final ages.

inputs.name: luminescence-age
inputs.desc: Final age estimate with uncertainty

inputs.name: age-model-assessment
inputs.desc: De distribution analysis and age model choice

inputs.name: sar-diagnostics
inputs.desc: SAR protocol quality checks

outputs.name: luminescence-report
outputs.desc: Full dating report with methods, results, and geological interpretation

outputs.name: luminescence-data-archive
outputs.desc: All measurement data, dose rates, and age calculations for archival

process: Present the De distributions as radial plots and histograms
Tabulate all dose rate components and total dose rates
Report final ages in their stratigraphic context with figures
Discuss any complications (partial bleaching, dose rate changes) and their effect on the ages

description: Monitor a process with multivariate statistical control from variable compilation through PCA modeling, control limit setting, batch monitoring, fault diagnosis, and reporting.

steps.description: Compile and preprocess the process variable matrix from historical normal operating data.

inputs.name: process-data-sources
inputs.desc: Historian databases, sensor logs, or batch records for the process

inputs.name: variable-selection
inputs.desc: List of process variables to include and their engineering units

outputs.name: process-matrix
outputs.desc: Cleaned, aligned time-series matrix of process variables for the reference period

outputs.name: variable-metadata
outputs.desc: Variable names, units, ranges, and any known correlations

process: Extract time-aligned process variable data from the historian for the reference (normal) period
Handle missing values by interpolation or exclusion based on gap length
Remove known abnormal periods (shutdowns, upsets, calibrations) from the reference dataset
Auto-scale each variable to zero mean and unit variance

steps.description: Build a PCA or PLS model from the reference process data to capture the normal correlation structure.

inputs.name: process-matrix
inputs.desc: Scaled process variable matrix for the reference period

inputs.name: model-selection-criteria
inputs.desc: Cross-validation method and number of components to evaluate

outputs.name: pca-model
outputs.desc: Fitted PCA or PLS model with loadings, scores, and retained components

outputs.name: model-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Explained variance, cross-validation results, and component selection rationale

process: Compute the PCA decomposition of the scaled process matrix
Select the number of retained components using cross-validation or scree plot
Examine loading plots to verify that the components capture meaningful process relationships
Compute model statistics (explained variance per component, Q residuals on the training set)

steps.description: Set T-squared and Q-residual control limits from the reference data using the appropriate statistical distributions.

inputs.name: pca-model
inputs.desc: Fitted PCA model from the reference period

inputs.name: confidence-level
inputs.desc: Desired confidence level for the control limits (typically 95% or 99%)

outputs.name: control-limits
outputs.desc: T-squared and Q-residual control limits at the specified confidence level

outputs.name: reference-control-charts
outputs.desc: Control charts of T-squared and Q for the reference data, confirming the limits capture normal variation

process: Compute the T-squared limit from the F-distribution for the number of components and observations
Compute the Q-residual limit from the Jackson-Mudholkar approximation or bootstrap
Plot the reference-period T-squared and Q values against the limits to verify coverage
Adjust if the reference data show non-normality that the limits do not accommodate

steps.description: Monitor new batch or continuous process data against the PCA model and control limits to detect out-of-control events.

inputs.name: new-process-data
inputs.desc: Incoming process variable data from the batch or stream being monitored

inputs.name: pca-model
inputs.desc: Fitted PCA model from reference data

inputs.name: control-limits
inputs.desc: T-squared and Q-residual limits

outputs.name: monitoring-results
outputs.desc: Time series of T-squared and Q values with alarm flags

outputs.name: alarm-log
outputs.desc: Timestamped list of control limit violations

process: Scale new observations using the reference-period means and standard deviations
Project onto the PCA model to compute T-squared and Q at each time point
Flag observations that exceed either control limit
Log alarm timestamps and durations for further investigation

steps.description: Diagnose which process variables contributed to each out-of-control event using contribution plots.

inputs.name: alarm-log
inputs.desc: Timestamped control limit violations

inputs.name: pca-model
inputs.desc: PCA model with loadings

inputs.name: new-process-data
inputs.desc: Process data during the alarm periods

outputs.name: contribution-plots
outputs.desc: Variable contributions to T-squared and Q at each alarm time

outputs.name: root-cause-candidates
outputs.desc: Ranked list of variables most responsible for each alarm event

process: Compute the contribution of each variable to the T-squared statistic at the alarm time
Compute the contribution of each variable to the Q residual at the alarm time
Rank variables by contribution magnitude to identify the probable root cause
Cross-reference with process knowledge to confirm the diagnosis

steps.description: Compile the multivariate process monitoring results into a report with control charts, contribution analysis, and recommendations.

inputs.name: monitoring-results
inputs.desc: T-squared and Q time series with alarms

inputs.name: contribution-plots
inputs.desc: Variable contributions for each alarm event

inputs.name: root-cause-candidates
inputs.desc: Diagnosed root causes

outputs.name: monitoring-report
outputs.desc: Process monitoring report with control charts, fault diagnosis, and recommendations

outputs.name: monitoring-data-archive
outputs.desc: Model, limits, monitoring data, and contribution analysis for archival

process: Generate control chart figures with alarm annotations
Compile contribution plots for each significant alarm event
Write a summary of detected faults, their root causes, and process impact
Recommend corrective actions or model updates based on the findings
